			"articleBody": "Bhubaneswar A dawn-to-dusk Odisha Bandh called by INDIA Bloc parties to protest the Mines and Minerals (Development and Regulation) Amendment Act, 2026, and demand the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over his involvement in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls evoked a mixed response on Thursday (October 8, 2026). INDIA Bloc parties, including the Congress and Left parties, were seen enforcing the bandh on the streets of Bhubaneswar, Cuttack, Berhampur and all major district headquarters towns. The parties had made it clear that ambulances and students travelling for examinations would be kept out of the purview of the bandh. BJD distances itself from Congress after withdrawing support for Odisha Bandh BJD distances itself from Congress after withdrawing support for Odisha Bandh Senior BJD leader and party Chief Whip Pramila Mallik backtracked on Odisha Bandh support within an hour after initially extending support for INDIA Bloc\u2019s call for Bandh on Thursday BJD distances itself from Congress after withdrawing support for Odisha Bandh storyline 1 However, business establishments remained closed along national and state highways and major arterial roads in the towns. There were no reports of violence, except for protesters halting passenger vehicles and enquiring about their destinations. As long-distance buses were parked safely at bus terminals in view of the shutdown, passengers were seen waiting for the impact of the bandh to ease. MoEF grants environmental, CRZ clearance for Puri\u2019s greenfield airport MoEF grants environmental, CRZ clearance for Puri\u2019s greenfield airport MoEF directs to prepare a bird hazard study from reputed institute in the field after a Wildlife Institute of India study flags the issue of risk posed by migratory birds from Chilika Lake MoEF grants environmental, CRZ clearance for Puri\u2019s greenfield airport storyline 1 \u201cThe Odisha Bandh observed on October 8 received an unprecedented response across the State, with the constituent parties of the INDIA Bloc coming together in Bhubaneswar to stage a strong and united protest,\u201d said Suresh Panigrahy, State secretary of the CPI(M). Mr Panigrahy said the CEC must step down after massive irregularities in the SIR exercise came to light and the entire country stood up against the Election Commission of India, whose credibility, he said, was now at an all-time low. \u201cAs far as Odisha is concerned, the MMDR Amendment Act has snatched away the State\u2019s right to impose tax on mineral extraction from its land. It will badly hit the economy of a mineral-rich State like Odisha in the long run,\u201d he pointed out. Protesters also demanded the resignation of School and Mass Education Minister Nityanand Gond over more than 1,700 errors detected in school textbooks prepared for Classes I to VIII. INDIA Bloc parties warned that their protest against alleged irregularities and what they described as anti-democratic steps by the BJP governments at the State and Centre would not end with the Odisha Bandh and would continue in the future.",

/* shorts page css */
.stories-list {
  list-style: none;
  margin: 30px auto;
  padding: 0;
  overflow-x: auto;
  white-space: nowrap;
  text-align: center;
}
.stories-list .storie-item {
  display: inline-block;
  vertical-align: top;
  width: 18%;
  border-radius: 8px;
  position: relative;
  overflow: hidden;
  margin: 0 8px;
  cursor: pointer;
}
.stories-list .storie-item .picture {
  width: 100%;
  min-height: unset;
  position: relative;
  --bs-aspect-ratio: calc(6 / 4 * 100%);
}
.stories-list .storie-item .picture::before {
  display: block;
  padding-top: var(--bs-aspect-ratio);
  content: "";
}
.stories-list .storie-item .picture > * {
  position: absolute;
  top: 0;
  left: 0;
  width: 100%;
  height: 100%;
}
.stories-list .storie-item .picture img {
  width: 100%;
  object-fit: cover;
  object-position: center;
  height: 100%;
  min-height: unset;
}
.stories-list .storie-item .picture .text-part {
  background: linear-gradient(
    0deg,
    rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.8),
    rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.6),
    rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.4),
    rgba(0, 0, 0, 0),
    rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.21),
    rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.66)
  );
  position: absolute;
  width: 100%;
  height: 100%;
  top: 0;
  left: 0;
}
.stories-list .storie-item .picture .text-part .past-stories {
  display: flex;
  position: absolute;
  bottom: 8px;
  left: 6px;
  right: 6px;
  z-index: 1;
  overflow: hidden;
}
.stories-list .storie-item .picture .text-part .past-stories span {
  height: 2px;
  border-radius: 4px;
  background-color: #fff;
  opacity: 0.4;
  margin-right: 3px;
  overflow: hidden;
  margin-top: 5px;
  margin-left: 3px;
  flex: 1;
}
.stories-list .storie-item .picture .text-part .past-stories span.active {
  opacity: 1;
}
.stories-list .storie-item .picture .icon-part {
  height: 30px;
  width: 30px;
  margin: 14px;
}
.stories-list .storie-item .picture .icon-part img {
  height: 30px;
  width: 30px;
}
.stories-list .storie-item .title {
  color: #000000;
  font-family: "Merriweather", serif;
  letter-spacing: 0.2px;
  font-size: 14px;
  text-align: left;
  padding: 15px 3px 0;
  position: relative;
  bottom: 10px;
  line-height: normal;
  white-space: normal;
}
.stories-list.inner-page {
  overflow-x: unset;
  white-space: unset;
  margin: unset;
  padding: unset;
  text-align: center;
  padding: 0px 10px 10px 10px;
}

  margin: 0px 8px 10px 8px;

                </a><span class="delete bookmarkdelete">

                </span></div></div></div><div class="right"><div id="article-top-right"></div></div></div><div class="article-picture top-pic "><div class="picture verticle"><picture><!--[if IE 9]><video style="display: none;"><![endif]--><source media="(min-width: 1600px)" sizes="960px" srcset="https://th-i.thgim.com/public/incoming/cyu06k/article71558490.ece/alternates/LANDSCAPE_1200/PTI09_29_2026_000302A.jpg"><source media="(min-width: 768px) and (max-width: 1599px)" sizes="640px" srcset="https://th-i.thgim.com/public/incoming/cyu06k/article71558490.ece/alternates/LANDSCAPE_1200/PTI09_29_2026_000302A.jpg"><source media="(min-width: 321px) and (max-width: 767px)" sizes="400px" srcset="https://th-i.thgim.com/public/incoming/cyu06k/article71558490.ece/alternates/LANDSCAPE_660/PTI09_29_2026_000302A.jpg"><source media="(max-width: 320px)" sizes="320px" srcset="https://th-i.thgim.com/public/incoming/cyu06k/article71558490.ece/alternates/LANDSCAPE_320/PTI09_29_2026_000302A.jpg"><!--[if IE 9]></video><![endif]--><img src="https://www.thehindu.com/theme/images/th-online/1x1_spacer.png" alt="Congress-led INDIA bloc workers and leaders stage a protest rally against the MMDR Amendment Act, in Bhubaneswar, September 29, 2026." title="Congress-led INDIA bloc workers and leaders stage a protest rally against the MMDR Amendment Act, in Bhubaneswar, September 29, 2026." data-original="https://www.thehindu.com/theme/images/th-online/1x1_spacer.png" class="lead-img" fetchpriority="high"></picture></div><p class="caption">
                    Congress-led INDIA bloc workers and leaders stage a protest rally against the MMDR Amendment Act, in Bhubaneswar, September 29, 2026.
                                          | Photo Credit: PTI
                                      </p></div><div id="content-body-71558469" class="articlebodycontent col-xl-9 col-lg-12 col-md-12 col-sm-12 col-12"><div class="schemaDiv" id="schemaDiv"><p>A dawn-to-dusk Odisha Bandh called by INDIA Bloc parties to protest the Mines and Minerals (Development and Regulation) Amendment Act, 2026, and demand the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over his involvement in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls evoked a mixed response on Thursday (October 8, 2026).</p><div class="article-ad"><div class="dfp-ad articleinlinead  middleonead" id="Desktop_AT_Mid01" style="min-height: 90px;"></div></div><p>INDIA Bloc parties, including the Congress and Left parties, were seen enforcing the bandh on the streets of Bhubaneswar, Cuttack, Berhampur and all major district headquarters towns. The parties had made it clear that ambulances and students travelling for examinations would be kept out of the purview of the bandh.</p><div class="" id="artmeterpv"></div><div class="also-read print-hide" data-ga-label="AlsoReadArticle"><div class="element"><div class="title"><a href="https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/odisha/bjd-distances-itself-from-congress-after-withdrawing-support-for-odisha-bandh/article71556470.ece">
										BJD distances itself from Congress after withdrawing support for Odisha Bandh</a></div><div class="picture"><img src="https://www.thehindu.com/theme/images/th-online/1x1_spacer.png" data-src-template="https://th-i.thgim.com/public/incoming/8h9iwq/article71558294.ece/alternates/SQUARE_80/OD-TEXBOOKS-PATGF4G6F270.3.jpg.jpg" data-original="https://th-i.thgim.com/public/incoming/8h9iwq/article71558294.ece/alternates/SQUARE_80/OD-TEXBOOKS-PATGF4G6F270.3.jpg.jpg" alt="" data-device-variant="SQUARE~SQUARE~SQUARE~SQUARE" class="media-object lazy adaptive placeholder lazy" width="100%" height="100%"></div></div></div><p>However, business establishments remained closed along national and state highways and major arterial roads in the towns. There were no reports of violence, except for protesters halting passenger vehicles and enquiring about their destinations.</p><div class="article-ad"><div class="dfp-ad articleinlinead" id="Desktop_Inarticle_1x1" style="min-height: 250px;"></div></div><p>As long-distance buses were parked safely at bus terminals in view of the shutdown, passengers were seen waiting for the impact of the bandh to ease.</p><div class="also-read print-hide" data-ga-label="AlsoReadArticle"><div class="element"><div class="title"><a href="https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/odisha/moef-grants-environmental-crz-clearance-for-puris-greenfield-airport/article71556220.ece">
										MoEF grants environmental, CRZ clearance for Puri’s greenfield airport</a></div><div class="picture"></div></div></div><p>“The Odisha Bandh observed on October 8 received an unprecedented response across the State, with the constituent parties of the INDIA Bloc coming together in Bhubaneswar to stage a strong and united protest,” said Suresh Panigrahy, State secretary of the CPI(M).</p><p>Mr Panigrahy said the CEC must step down after massive irregularities in the SIR exercise came to light and the entire country stood up against the Election Commission of India, whose credibility, he said, was now at an all-time low.</p><div class="article-ad"><div class="dfp-ad articleinlinead" id="Desktop_AT_Mid02" style="min-height: 90px;"></div></div><p>“As far as Odisha is concerned, the MMDR Amendment Act has snatched away the State’s right to impose tax on mineral extraction from its land. It will badly hit the economy of a mineral-rich State like Odisha in the long run,” he pointed out.</p><p>Protesters also demanded the resignation of School and Mass Education Minister Nityanand Gond over more than 1,700 errors detected in school textbooks prepared for Classes I to VIII. INDIA Bloc parties warned that their protest against alleged irregularities and what they described as anti-democratic steps by the BJP governments at the State and Centre would not end with the Odisha Bandh and would continue in the future.</p></div><div class="articleblock-container" id="arthardpv"></div><div class="update-publish-time article-published-time-end"><p class="publish-time-new"> Published <span>- October 08, 2026 10:57 am IST</span></p></div><button class="btn comments comment-btn print-hide">

     }, "articleSection" : "Nation",
    "articleBody" : "Bhubaneswar: Normal life was disrupted across Odisha on Thursday as the Congress-led INDIA bloc enforced a 12-hour statewide bandh, with buses and autorickshaws staying off the roads, shops and markets remaining closed and road and mining operations affected at several places.    The bandh, observed from 6 am to 6 pm, was called over four major demands — withdrawal of the MMDR Amendment Act, 2026, resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over alleged irregularities in the electoral roll revision, resignation of school and mass education minister Nityananda Gond over alleged errors in school textbooks, and immediate relief for flood-affected families.    The impact was particularly visible in Bhubaneswar, Cuttack, Sambalpur, Bhadrak and several other districts. In the capital, protesters blocked roads at several locations, while bus and autorickshaw movement came to a halt at Master Canteen. Additional police personnel were deployed across the city, with around 18 platoons and 100 officers kept ready to maintain law and order.    Public transport remained the biggest casualty. Although the state private bus owners’ association had not extended support to the bandh, services were disrupted at several places amid picketing and road blockades. The Nikhila Utkal Auto Chalak Sangha kept autorickshaws off the roads, citing security concerns.    Several passengers were left stranded. In Cuttack, a group of five persons who had visited Puri said they could not return home after finding no buses. A surgeon heading to Capital Hospital in Bhubaneswar was also reportedly stopped by protesters before being allowed to proceed after explaining that he had scheduled surgeries.    The bandh had a major impact on the mining belt of Sundargarh. At Koida, protesters blocked the main intersection, halting mineral transportation from several mines. Railway sidings remained closed and goods trains were reportedly stopped, while mining operations, shops and markets were shut.    In Malkangiri, schools, shops and markets remained closed and vehicular movement was disrupted across all seven blocks.    In Sambalpur, women Congress leaders adopted an unusual form of picketing at the Collectorate, handing flowers to employees and urging them to stop work.    PCC president Bhakta Charan Das claimed the bandh had received widespread public support, while BJP leaders alleged that Congress workers were forcing people to participate.    “We are thankful to the people of Odisha for extending whole-hearted support to our bandh call. It implies that they are with us to protect the democratic values of the country,” said Das.    Essential services, including hospitals, ambulances, fire and rescue services, medicine shops, milk supply, examinations and media operations, remained exempt from the shutdown. d-paira-cover"><div class="story_content details-story-wrapper details-content-story article_cont_size"><div itemprop="articleBody" class="entry-main-content dropcap"><p><b>Bhubaneswar</b>: Normal life was disrupted across Odisha on Thursday as the Congress-led INDIA bloc enforced a 12-hour statewide bandh, with buses and autorickshaws staying off the roads, shops and markets remaining closed and road and mining operations affected at several places.  </p><p>  </p><p>The bandh, observed from 6 am to 6 pm, was called over four major demands — withdrawal of the MMDR Amendment Act, 2026, resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over alleged irregularities in the electoral roll revision, resignation of school and mass education minister Nityananda Gond over alleged errors in school textbooks, and immediate relief for flood-affected families.  </p><div class="hide inside-post-ad-before-before" id="inside_post_content_ad_1_before_before"></div><div class="hide inside-post-ad-before" id="inside_post_content_ad_1_before"></div><div class="hide inside-post-ad-1 inside-post-ad ads_common_inside_post" id="inside_post_content_ad_1"></div><div class="hide inside-post-ad-after" id="inside_post_content_ad_1_after"></div><p>  </p><p>The impact was particularly visible in Bhubaneswar, Cuttack, Sambalpur, Bhadrak and several other districts. </p><p>In the capital, protesters blocked roads at several locations, while bus and autorickshaw movement came to a halt at Master Canteen.</p><p> Additional police personnel were deployed across the city, with around 18 platoons and 100 officers kept ready to maintain law and order.  </p><p>  </p><p>Public transport remained the biggest casualty.</p><div class="hide inside-post-ad-before-before" id="inside_post_content_ad_2_before_before"></div><div class="hide inside-post-ad-before" id="inside_post_content_ad_2_before"></div><div class="hide inside-post-ad-2 inside-post-ad ads_common_inside_post" id="inside_post_content_ad_2"></div><div class="hide inside-post-ad-after" id="inside_post_content_ad_2_after"></div><p> Although the state private bus owners’ association had not extended support to the bandh, services were disrupted at several places amid picketing and road blockades. </p><p>The Nikhila Utkal Auto Chalak Sangha kept autorickshaws off the roads, citing security concerns.  </p><p>  </p><p>Several passengers were left stranded. </p><p>In Cuttack, a group of five persons who had visited Puri said they could not return home after finding no buses.</p><div class="hide inside-post-ad-before-before" id="inside_post_content_ad_3_before_before"></div><div class="hide inside-post-ad-before" id="inside_post_content_ad_3_before"></div><div class="hide inside-post-ad-3 inside-post-ad ads_common_inside_post" id="inside_post_content_ad_3"></div><div class="hide inside-post-ad-after" id="inside_post_content_ad_3_after"></div><p> A surgeon heading to Capital Hospital in Bhubaneswar was also reportedly stopped by protesters before being allowed to proceed after explaining that he had scheduled surgeries.  </p><p>  </p><p>The bandh had a major impact on the mining belt of Sundargarh.</p><p> At Koida, protesters blocked the main intersection, halting mineral transportation from several mines. </p><p>Railway sidings remained closed and goods trains were reportedly stopped, while mining operations, shops and markets were shut.  </p><div class="hide inside-post-ad-before-before" id="inside_post_content_ad_4_before_before"></div><div class="hide inside-post-ad-before" id="inside_post_content_ad_4_before"></div><div class="hide inside-post-ad-4 inside-post-ad ads_common_inside_post" id="inside_post_content_ad_4"></div><div class="hide inside-post-ad-after" id="inside_post_content_ad_4_after"></div><p>  </p><p>In Malkangiri, schools, shops and markets remained closed and vehicular movement was disrupted across all seven blocks.  </p><p>  </p><p>In Sambalpur, women Congress leaders adopted an unusual form of picketing at the Collectorate, handing flowers to employees and urging them to stop work.  </p><p>  </p><p>PCC president Bhakta Charan Das claimed the bandh had received widespread public support, while BJP leaders alleged that Congress workers were forcing people to participate.  </p><div class="hide inside-post-ad filler-ad-unit-inside-post" id="filler_ad"></div><p>  </p><p>“We are thankful to the people of Odisha for extending whole-hearted support to our bandh call. </p><p>It implies that they are with us to protect the democratic values of the country,” said Das.  </p><p>  </p><p>Essential services, including hospitals, ambulances, fire and rescue services, medicine shops, milk supply, examinations and media operations, remained exempt from the shutdown.  </p><p>  </p><p><br></p><p>  </p><p>Photograph: Congress-led INDIA bloc workers stage a protest in Bhubaneswar on Thursday during the observance of the party’s 12-hour bandh call in Odisha.</p></div></div></div></div><div id="ad_level_3_before" class=" hide"></div><div id="left_level_3_before" class=" hide"></div><div <script>
(function () {


const SITES = [
    { name: "Dinamani", url: "https://www.dinamani.com" },
    { name: "Kannada Prabha", url: "https://www.kannadaprabha.com" },
    { name: "Samakalika Malayalam", url: "https://www.samakalikamalayalam.com" },
    { name: "Cinema Express", url: "https://www.cinemaexpress.com" },
    { name: "Indulgexpress", url: "https://www.indulgexpress.com" },
    { name: "Edexlive", url: "https://www.edexlive.com" }
];


function init() {


    if (document.getElementById("network-strip")) return;
    const navbar = document.querySelector("#navbar");
    if (!navbar) return;
    const style = document.createElement("style");
    style.innerHTML = `
#network-strip{
    width:100%;
    background:#fff;
    border-bottom:1px solid #e5e5e5;
    overflow:hidden;
    font-family:system-ui,-apple-system,BlinkMacSystemFont,"Segoe UI",Roboto,sans-serif;
    box-sizing:border-box;
}


#network-strip .network-scroll{
    overflow-x:auto;
    overflow-y:hidden;
    -webkit-overflow-scrolling:touch;
    scrollbar-width:none;
    touch-action:pan-x;
    scroll-behavior:smooth;
}


#network-strip .network-scroll::-webkit-scrollbar{
    display:none;
}


#network-strip .network-list{
    display:flex;
    align-items:center;
    justify-content:center;
    list-style:none;
    margin:0;
    padding:8px 20px;
    white-space:nowrap;
    width:max-content;
    min-width:100%;
}


#network-strip .network-list li{
    display:flex;
    align-items:center;
    flex:0 0 auto;
}


#network-strip .network-list li:not(:last-child)::after{
    content:"|";
    color:#bdbdbd;
    margin:0 14px;
}


#network-strip .network-list a{
    color:#555;
    text-decoration:none;
    font-size:15px;
    font-weight:500;
    transition:.2s;
}


#network-strip .network-list a:hover{
    color:#000;
}


@media(max-width:768px){


    #network-strip .network-list{
        justify-content:flex-start;
        min-width:max-content;
        padding:8px 16px;
    }


    #network-strip .network-list a{
        font-size:12px;
    }


    #network-strip .network-list li:not(:last-child)::after{
        margin:0 10px;
    }


}
`;


    document.head.appendChild(style);


    const strip = document.createElement("div");
    strip.id = "network-strip";


    const scroll = document.createElement("div");
    scroll.className = "network-scroll";


    const ul = document.createElement("ul");
    ul.className = "network-list";


    SITES.forEach(site => {


        const li = document.createElement("li");


        const a = document.createElement("a");
        a.href = site.url;
        a.target = "_blank";
        a.rel = "noopener noreferrer";
        a.textContent = site.name;


        li.appendChild(a);
        ul.appendChild(li);


    });


    scroll.appendChild(ul);
    strip.appendChild(scroll);


    navbar.prepend(strip);


}


if (document.readyState === "loading") {
    document.addEventListener("DOMContentLoaded", init);
} else {
    init();
}


})();

</div></div></div><div class="arr--element-container story-element-card-m_element-container__1ZeJL story-element-card-m_dark__1AX15"><div data-test-id="text" class="arrow-component arr--text-element text-m_textElement__e3QEt text-m_dark__1TC18 " style="color: rgb(51, 51, 51);"><p>BHUBANESWAR: The Odisha government on Wednesday directed all collectors to take preventive measures to avoid any untoward incident during the 12-hour Odisha bandh called by the INDIA bloc.</p><p>In a letter to all collectors, the Home department said the statewide bandh may witness road blockades, rallies, demonstrations, roko and forceful closure of mines, government offices, educational institutions, markets and commercial establishments across the state.</p><p>The collectors have been asked to take preventive and precautionary measures to maintain law and order and keep a close vigil to ensure that no untoward incident takes place. Arrangements should also be made for the smooth functioning of central and state government offices and essential services across the state.</p><p>Odisha Police said efforts will be made to ensure that everything remains open for the public. Bhubaneswar DCP Saravana Vivek M said police are prepared to maintain law and order during the bandh. “About 100 officers and 18 platoons of police force will be deployed across the capital city to ensure citizens do not face any inconvenience,” he said.</p><p>The bandh has been called by the INDIA bloc demanding revocation of the MMDR Amendment Act, 2026, resignation of chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and School and Mass Education minister Nityananda Gond, as well as immediate relief for flood-affected victims. The 6 am to 6 pm bandh is likely to impact transport services the most. </p></div></div><div class="arr--element-container story-element-card-m_element-container__1ZeJL story-element-card-m_dark__1AX15"><div id="widget-inreads_1x1-b0a5b9fb-d90b-4af1-982a-30159e58dd70" data-test-id="widget" class="app-ad app-ad--story-horizontal widget-m__widget__bUJP1" style="--widget-height-mobile: 220px; --widget-height-desktop: 360px;"><div style="height: 50px;"></div></div></div></div><div class="arr--story-page-card-wrapper"><div class="arr--element-container story-element-card-m_element-container__1ZeJL story-element-card-m_dark__1AX15"><div data-test-id="text" class="arrow-component arr--text-element text-m_textElement__e3QEt text-m_dark__1TC18 " style="color: rgb(51, 51, 51);"><p>The Capital Region Urban Transport (CRUT) said though Ama Buses will continue to operate during the bandh, services on some routes might be cancelled or diverted depending on the scale of the protests.</p><p>The All Odisha Private Bus Owners’ Association said it wants to continue its services but expressed apprehension that transport operations might be affected by the strike. Association president Loknath Pani said thousands of passengers depend on buses and operators want to continue services as usual. “However, operations might get disrupted if protesters block highways and major roads,” he added.</p><p>General secretary of the Bhubaneswar Auto-rickshaw Mahasangh Padman Samal said the body would not risk operating its vehicles during the strike. “Who will be responsible if our vehicles are targeted during the protests?” he questioned. Most educational institutions, petrol pumps and commercial establishments at prominent locations in the city are expected to remain closed.</p></div></div><div class="arr--element-container story-element-card-m_element-container__1ZeJL story-element-card-m_dark__1AX15"><div data-test-id="promotional-message" class="arrow-component arr--text-element text-m_promotionalMessage__CUsPM text-m_dark__1TC18 "><div><p><strong><ins><a aria-label="content" target="_self" href="https://www.whatsapp.com/channel/0029VaAJz0Q2f3EFfUEev01O">Follow The New Indian Express channel on WhatsApp</a> </ins></strong></p><p><strong><a aria-label="content" target="_self" href="https://onelink.to/heh8j3">Download the TNIE app to stay with us and follow the latest</a></strong></p><p></p></div></div></div><div class="arr--element-container story-element-card-m_element-container__1ZeJL story-element-card-m_dark__1AX15"><div id="widget-2_eadd7cd4-11b2-49e5-b817-34381d25d8a9" data-test-id="widget" class="app-ad app-ad--story-horizontal widget-m__widget__bUJP1" style="--widget-height-mobile: 250px; The Odisha government on Wednesday directed all collectors to take preventive measures to avoid any untoward incident during the 12-hour Odisha bandh called by the INDIA bloc.\u003C\u002Fp\u003E\u003Cp\u003EIn a letter to all collectors, the Home department said the statewide bandh may witness road blockades, rallies, demonstrations, roko and forceful closure of mines, government offices, educational institutions, markets and commercial establishments across the state.\u003C\u002Fp\u003E\u003Cp\u003EThe collectors have been asked to take preventive and precautionary measures to maintain law and order and keep a close vigil to ensure that no untoward incident takes place. Arrangements should also be made for the smooth functioning of central and state government offices and essential services across the state.\u003C\u002Fp\u003E\u003Cp\u003EOdisha Police said efforts will be made to ensure that everything remains open for the public. Bhubaneswar DCP Saravana Vivek M said police are prepared to maintain law and order during the bandh. “About 100 officers and 18 platoons of police force will be deployed across the capital city to ensure citizens do not face any inconvenience,” he said.\u003C\u002Fp\u003E\u003Cp\u003EThe bandh has been called by the INDIA bloc demanding revocation of the MMDR Amendment Act, 2026, resignation of chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and School and Mass Education minister Nityananda Gond, as well as immediate relief for flood-affected victims. several districts of Odisha on Thursday as INDIA bloc parties observed a 12-hour bandh from 6 am to 6 pm to protest the new mining law, alleged errors in school textbooks and alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.Supporters of the Congress, CPI, CPI(M), CPI(ML) Liberation, Forward Bloc, NCP (Sharad Pawar), Samajwadi Party, RJD and JMM staged demonstrations and blocked roads at several places, including Bhubaneswar, Cuttack, Bargarh, Bhadrak, Balasore, Rayagada, Kendrapara, Bolangir, Berhampur and Sambalpur.Protesters also stopped buses, trucks, taxis and autorickshaws at several locations and burnt tyres, disrupting traffic movement.Shops, business establishments, petrol pumps and several educational institutions remained closed in parts of the state, while public transport services were hit.Many commuters were left waiting at bus stops, with office-goers, students and others facing difficulties in reaching their destinations. Auto-rickshaw services were also affected in some areas.In Bhubaneswar, the Capital Region Urban Transport (CRUT) said Ama Bus services were intended to operate, though services on some routes could be affected depending on the situation.Essential services, including hospitals, ambulances, fire services, pharmacies and milk supply, were kept outside the purview of the bandh, a Congress leader said.The INDIA bloc has demanded the repeal of the MMDR (Amendment) Act, the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over alleged "vote chori" and the resignation of state minister Nityananda Gond over alleged errors in school textbooks."We demand a complete rollback of the MMDR (Amendment) Act, resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar for 'vote chori' and state minister Nityananda Gond for distributing books with erroneous information among school students," senior Congress leader Suresh Routray said in Bhubaneswar.Police deployed adequate security across the state to prevent any untoward incidents and said efforts were being made to ensure that the demonstrations remained peaceful and within the ambit of constitutional rights.Bhubaneswar-Cuttack Odisha Bandh on October 8: Transport, Markets May Be Affected

The INDIA bloc is set to observe a statewide bandh in Odisha on Thursday, October 8, 2026, over three key demands. The protest call may affect normal life, with road transport, markets and business establishments likely to face disruptions in several parts of the state.

Congress and its alliance partners are expected to stage demonstrations and road blockades across Odisha. Commuters may face traffic congestion and delays, particularly in major cities and towns. Some shops and commercial establishments may also remain closed, depending on local participation.

Protesters may organise rail roko demonstrations at railway stations, potentially affecting train services. The extent of the disruption is expected to vary across locations.

Emergency Services to Remain Exempt

Essential and emergency services, including ambulances, fire services, pharmacies, milk transportation and other emergency facilities, are expected to remain exempt from the bandh.

Three Key Demands Behind the Bandh

The INDIA bloc has called the bandh over the following demands:

  • Withdrawal of the MMDR Amendment Act, 2026: Opposition parties are demanding the immediate withdrawal of the legislation.
  • Resignation of Odisha’s School and Mass Education Minister Nityananda Gond: The demand follows allegations of errors in school textbooks.
  • Action against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar: The opposition is seeking his resignation and arrest over alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) exercise.

The opposition parties have said the bandh is intended to pressure the government to address these issues.

Odisha Pradesh Congress Committee president Bhakta Charan Das said Congress and its alliance partners would work to ensure that the bandh is observed peacefully across the state.

Residents are advised to check local transport updates and official announcements before travelling, as the impact may differ across districts.
